hints: With the shortcut in, look at bulb B's current reading. Where did the current go instead?

Current splits between the paths it can take, and more of it goes the easier way. A bare wire has almost no resistance, so nearly all the current skips bulb B. The loop now has less resistance, so more current flows through bulb A.
Run it with the shortcut wire in, then take it out, and compare bulb A both times.
